questions.stem_text: Markings found on the mud-bricks of Huaca del Sol are probably:

options.A: instructions for the builders written there by the engineers.
options.B: random scratches and not a meaningful script or written language.
options.C: intended to identify the local group that had produced them.
options.D: simple arithmetic performed by carpenters on the building site.

questions.answer_explanation: The markings on the mud-bricks of Huaca del Sol likely served as identifiers for the local groups, reflecting their cultural practices and social organization in the context of pre-Columbian societies.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is not a hypothesis for why hominids walked on two legs?

options.A: it expended less energy than quadrupedalism for going long distances
options.B: it freed the hands to carry things
options.C: it allowed hominids to see greater distances
options.D: it provided a more intimidating posture to potential predators
options.E: it allowed for better heat regulation

questions.answer_explanation: The statement is correct because it inaccurately suggests that bipedalism is more energy-efficient for long distances compared to quadrupedalism, whereas research indicates that while bipedalism has advantages, quadrupedalism is generally more energy-efficient for long-distance travel.

options.D: reliance on food storage and preservation.
options.E: focusing on one specific type of food source.

questions.answer_explanation: Opportunistic foraging involves increased use of imported or "exotic" materials because it reflects a strategy where communities adapt their subsistence practices by integrating diverse resources from outside their immediate environment to enhance food security and nutritional variety.

questions.stem_text:
Which of the following dating techniques are based on the measurement of the amount of
energy trapped in materials that have been heated at archaeological sites?

options.B: tephrochronology and electron spin resonance dating
options.D: isotope-ratio mass spectrometry and fission track dating

questions.answer_explanation: Carbon-14 and uranium series dating are correct because both techniques rely on measuring the radioactive decay of isotopes that accumulate in materials, which effectively indicates the time elapsed since those materials were last heated.

questions.stem_text:
In comparison to Homo habilis, what gave Homo erectus the ability to migrate so far, so
fast?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer, microcephaly, suggests a neurological adaptation that may have contributed to the cognitive abilities and physical adaptations of Homo erectus, enabling them to develop tools, navigate diverse environments, and migrate over long distances more effectively than Homo habilis.
